The disk filled up and took the api down: the `report-export` job wrote 40 CSV parts of 512 MB each (about 20 GB) into `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` between 03:05:00 and 03:12:48, on the same volume Postgres uses.

The disk warning hit 91% at 03:09:03 and 99% at 03:13:30. At 03:14:00 the db failed with `could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device`, the api aborted its transaction and shut down its worker pool at 03:14:03, and it exited with status 1 at 03:14:06.

The api never came back within this log. The proxy logs `upstream api refused connection` every two minutes from 03:16:00 through 05:28:00 (67 times), and there are no api request lines after 03:13:51 up to the end of the log at 05:29:57. Web and proxy kept serving 200s throughout. The periodic `cache: slow command` warnings run from the first line onward at a steady cadence and are unrelated.

To recover, free space by clearing or moving `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, then check that the db is healthy and start the api. To stop it happening again, point the export at a different volume from the database or cap and clean up its output.

One thing to check: the entries in this log are all dated 2026-03-09, not last night, so confirm this is the right file for the outage you mean.
